messages.content: Change the split to two nights in Portland and five on the coast. Compare Camden, Rockland, and Boothbay Harbor, and make sure every room genuinely sleeps the three of us.

I found workable rooms for July 12-19 with Saturday as the transfer day. I am checking the displayed three-person occupancy against the actual bed description, then adding tax, parking, cancellation terms, and the transfer drive. Do you want central Portland only, or should I include the airport area if it saves enough?
Central Portland. We only have two nights there, so I do not want to commute into town.

For Portland, the strongest two are Canopy by Hilton Portland Waterfront and Hyatt Place Portland-Old Port. Canopy has a confirmed two-queen room for three: $918 room total, $82.62 tax, and $76 valet parking for two nights, or $1,076.62 altogether. There is no destination fee. It can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. July 9.
And the Hyatt?

Hyatt Place has a king room with a full-size pullout sofa, and the room record specifically lists one king plus sofa bed rather than just an occupancy limit of three. Two nights are $798, tax is $71.82, and valet parking is $80, for $949.82 total. No resort fee. Cancellation is free until 11:59 p.m. July 10.
That saves about $125. Is there any meaningful downside beyond not having two standard beds?

The Hyatt room is a little less comfortable once the sofa is opened, and recent room details put it at about 325 square feet versus roughly 390 at Canopy. Both are well placed for the Old Port. Canopy is quieter and has the better room configuration; Hyatt is the practical value choice for only two nights.
All right. Give me the coastal comparison, including the drives from Portland.

Camden: Camden Riverhouse has a two-queen room confirmed for three. Five nights are $1,945 plus $175.05 tax, totaling $2,120.05. Parking is included and there is no resort fee. Free cancellation runs through 6:00 p.m. July 5; after that, the first night is charged. The drive from central Portland is about 1 hour 50 minutes without a long stop.
How central is it, and what would we gain by paying more for Camden?

It is a short walk to the harbor and village center, so you can park once for dinner and the waterfront. Camden gives you the easiest access to Mount Battie and the most attractive evening setting of the three, while still putting Rockland about 20 minutes away. The tradeoff is the highest nightly cost among the practical non-resort options.
Now Rockland.

Hampton Inn & Suites Rockland has a two-queen room for three at $1,725 for five nights, plus $155.25 tax, totaling $1,880.25. Breakfast and parking are included, with no additional property fee. It is cancelable until 6:00 p.m. July 10. Portland to the hotel is about 1 hour 40 minutes. It is not in the prettiest part of town, but downtown Rockland is roughly a five-minute drive and Camden is about 15 to 20 minutes north.
That sounds more practical. What did you find in Boothbay Harbor?

Spruce Point Inn has a room with two queens and accepts three guests. Five nights are $2,410 plus $216.90 tax, totaling $2,626.90; self-parking is included. The restrictive point is cancellation: it is refundable only through June 28, and after that the deposit is forfeited. Portland to Boothbay Harbor is about 1 hour 15 minutes, but Boothbay to Rockland or Camden is generally 1 hour 20 minutes to 1 hour 40 minutes each way.
So it is quicker on transfer day but worse for seeing the rest of the midcoast.

Correct. Boothbay is appealing if the harbor and nearby boat trips are the center of the five days. For a broader trip that includes Camden, Rockland, lighthouses, and Mount Battie, it creates repeated backtracking. It is also $506.85 more than Camden Riverhouse and $746.65 more than the Hampton before any differences in meals.
Build the two combinations you would actually keep. Include everything for all seven hotel nights, not just the room rates.

Combination A, best value: Hyatt Place Portland-Old Port for July 12-14, then Hampton Inn & Suites Rockland for July 14-19. Portland is $949.82 including tax and parking; Rockland is $1,880.25 including tax with free parking. Seven-night lodging total: $2,830.07. The transfer is about 1 hour 40 minutes, and the later cancellation deadlines are July 10 at 11:59 p.m. for Hyatt and July 10 at 6:00 p.m. for Hampton.
And the version that prioritizes the nicer stay?

Combination B, strongest experience: Canopy Portland Waterfront for July 12-14, then Camden Riverhouse for July 14-19. Canopy is $1,076.62 including tax and parking; Camden is $2,120.05 including tax and free parking. Seven-night lodging total: $3,196.67. Transfer time is about 1 hour 50 minutes. The cancellation deadlines are July 9 at 6:00 p.m. for Canopy and July 5 at 6:00 p.m. for Camden.
That is a $366.60 difference. Is Camden worth that over Rockland for five nights?

Not entirely on lodging quality. Part of the difference buys Canopy's two standard beds and larger room in Portland. On the coast, Camden Riverhouse costs $239.80 more than the Hampton. Camden is worth that if walkable evenings and being beside the harbor matter heavily; Rockland offers the better operational base, easier parking, a later cancellation deadline, and short drives to Camden.
Give me your conclusion and what we need to decide next. Do not reserve either one.

Keep both combinations unreserved, but use Hyatt plus Hampton Rockland as the leading plan at $2,830.07 for all seven nights. Rockland gives the best balance of lodging practicality and access: it is less expensive, has a verified two-queen setup, includes parking, and remains close enough for multiple Camden visits without making every outing a long drive. Keep Canopy plus Camden as the experience upgrade at $3,196.67. Drop Boothbay Harbor from the final pair because its $3,576.72 total with Hyatt, early cancellation cutoff, and longer drives to Camden and Rockland do not fit this itinerary as well. Next, compare the exact ORD-PWM and ORD-BOS schedules and full trip costs for July 12-19; that will determine whether Portland should remain first and how much usable time each airport leaves on arrival and departure days.
